title: Rep. Ilhan Omar Forced to Relocate Following Federal Search and Escalating Death Threats
snippet: Minnesota Congresswoman Ilhan Omar says she must vacate her Washington residence due to safety fears after federal agents executed a search warrant at her home as part of an immigration probe.
content:
Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) announced she is vacating her Washington, D.C., apartment following a flood of death threats triggered by a federal search of her residence last week.

Speaking during an interview on MS NOW with Chris Hayes, the Minnesota lawmaker explained that her public address and escalating security risks have made it unfeasible to remain in the home, particularly with her children visiting. Omar recounted waking up early on Oct. 12 to find federal agents surrounding her house. Agents presented a search warrant, systematically searched her residence, and seized 17 items, including her smartphone and other electronics.

Targeted Investigation and Political Controversy

The search is connected to an immigration probe pushed by President Donald Trump and his allies, who claim Omar’s father submitted false information about her age when her family gained U.S. citizenship in 2000 after emigrating from Somalia. Omar has repeatedly denied the allegations, characterizing the investigation as a orchestrated campaign of political intimidation.

Previous reviews of her immigration records by federal officials under the first Trump administration in 2019 found no evidence of fraud. Questioning the tactics used against her, Omar noted that if authorities genuinely believed a crime had occurred, standard legal avenues like grand jury subpoenas would have been used rather than a sudden early-morning raid.

Oval Office Attacks and Democratic Backing

Trump maintained his aggressive stance against the congresswoman, telling reporters in the Oval Office on Wednesday that Omar is a "sick, very dishonest person" who despises the United States. In response, high-profile Democrats have rallied to her defense, including former President Barack Obama, who condemned the administration's probe as "appalling."

Addressing the ongoing public attacks, Omar expressed appreciation for the support from her colleagues and emphasized that she remains confident in her innocence, pledging to stand up against political bullying as the process unfolds.
